judgments.label: Health-relevant displacement share
judgments.basis: Subjective transfer: a legal outcome may delay or alter a move without preventing health-relevant displacement. The July2026 Memphis trial found no effect on ultimate residential stability, so the central scenario credits only a minority. This is not a measured fraction.

judgments.label: Utility gain among affected adults
judgments.basis: Subjective modest health-improvement scenario, not an eviction-specific preference-based study estimate. The search did not identify a measured coefficient; adjacent housing utility studies are often null.

judgments.label: Duration
judgments.basis: One-year window limits extrapolation. Judge-assignment evidence supports some first-year acute-health effects but not a persistent second-year utilization effect.

judgments.label: Affected adults
judgments.basis: One adult avoids unsupported household/child multipliers; it does not imply that other household members receive no benefit.

judgments.label: Donor additionality
judgments.basis: Central assumes the gift funds additional full-scope cases, not replacement of public funding. This is unverified. Zero additionality produces no finite price.

bottomLine: Our best guess for the narrow adult-health pathway is $126 million per 10 QALYs, conditional on extra cases and a positive legal effect. We would not prioritize this program on the present QALY estimate; justice, voice, financial protection and other non-health benefits are not fully represented. This is not evidence that legal assistance has no value.
nullBoundary: Zero legal effect, zero health effect or zero donor additionality means no finite cost per QALY; harm remains possible. Positive scenarios are not confidence intervals.
